sections.title: Biology and biomedicine on arXiv — 27 November 2026
sections.summary: Ten notable recent papers in the 19–26 November window, spanning DNA–protein kinetics, perturbation modeling, RNA design, and red-cell adhesion; attention evidence is sparse and arXiv coverage is incomplete.

sections.title: Exclusion and internal structure in the association/dissociation kinetics of DNA-binding proteins in the fast diffusion limit
sections.abstract: A coarse-grained stochastic/mean-field model combines DNA-site exclusion and protein conformational switching, is fitted to previously measured RPA–ssDNA dynamics, and extends to multisegment binding and facilitated exchange.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that their reduced Markov model captures stochastic coverage dynamics in tested fast-diffusion regimes and fits existing RPA binding data; the model also describes facilitated exchange in multisegment systems.
sections.unique_caveat: The central reduction assumes rapid positional equilibration; the RPA comparison refits prior experimental data rather than reporting a new biochemical experiment. The authors identify slower diffusion and active remodeling as open extensions.

sections.title: Receptor Abundance Alone Underpredicts Red Blood Cell Adhesion in Gaucher Disease
sections.comment: 25 pages, 9 figures. Supplementary Materials (32 pages) and Movies S1 and S2 are ancillary files
sections.abstract: A stochastic-bond red-cell model calibrated on control donors finds that the observed 1.3-fold Lu/BCAM increase does not explain the stronger adhesion reported for Gaucher-disease cells, pointing to receptor state as a possible additional factor.
sections.claimed_contribution: Using published adhesion measurements and a model calibrated to control donors, the authors report a 1.6–1.7-fold gap between measured and predicted adhesion and propose binding-competent receptor state, not abundance alone, as a plausible explanation.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a model-based analysis of existing donor and assay data, not a prospective clinical study. The paper notes assumptions including short simulated flow exposure and uncertain cell contact density; its donor groups numbered 12–23 per group.

sections.title: How Far Can Linear Go? BiPert, a Unified Framework for Single-Cell Perturbation Modelling
sections.abstract: BiPert uses a linear decomposition for forward prediction of perturbation responses and inverse identification of perturbed genes, with reported strengths on held-out cell lines and donors in published CRISPR-screen benchmarks.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report improved transfer on unseen cell lines over knowledge-free baselines and strong inverse identification on new contexts, with a few-shot variant using as few as ten measured perturbations.
sections.unique_caveat: Results are benchmark-based, not experimental validation of new gene mechanisms. On the full 34-view ExPert benchmark, ExPert slightly leads overall (top-10 recall 0.482 vs 0.449); BiPert's advantage concentrates in genuinely unseen lines or donors.

sections.title: Motivo: A Motif-Based Algorithm-Architecture Co-Design for Fast and Energy-Efficient Graph-Based Genome Analysis
sections.abstract: Motivo uses recurring genome-graph motifs to reduce redundant sequence-to-graph mapping work, with CPU, GPU, and proposed ASIC implementations evaluated on short- and long-read mapping tasks.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report speed, energy, and throughput gains over named graph-mapping baselines while maintaining 96.8–99.7% mapping accuracy on two types of genome graphs.
sections.unique_caveat: This is an algorithm/architecture benchmark, not evidence of improved biological conclusions in downstream studies; the reported results are tied to tested graph types, reads, and comparators.

sections.title: KnitNet: Learning to Search at Inference Time for Exact RNA Inverse Design
sections.abstract: KnitNet iteratively repairs candidate sequences using verifier feedback and an online surrogate; the authors report higher exact-match rates on five RNA secondary-structure benchmarks and improved 3D self-consistency.
sections.claimed_contribution: Across five secondary-structure benchmarks, the authors report a 21-percentage-point average exact-solve gain over continued sampling with 70% less time-to-solve; they also report improved 3D structural self-consistency versus per-target reinforcement learning.
sections.unique_caveat: The exact-match results are computational benchmarks; the reported 3D metric is structural self-consistency, not experimental confirmation that designed RNA folds as intended in vitro or in cells.

sections.title: From the Deterministic Hook Effect to Stochastic Reliability in Ternary Complex Formation
sections.abstract: Deterministic and stochastic simulations of a minimal reversible binding network show that a favorable average hook-shaped dose response need not yield reliable ternary-complex formation in small volumes.
sections.claimed_contribution: The author reports that volume, molecular copy-number thresholds, and complex formation/breakup rates change reliability even where deterministic dose-response favors assembly.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a minimal model with simulations, not an experimental test of a particular signaling pathway or therapeutic degrader.

sections.title: Cell-Type-Specific Expression Is Hard to Predict from Bulk, but It Is Still Useful
sections.comment: Accepted at the NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on AI for Drug Discovery (AI4DD). 5 pages main text, 28 pages total
sections.abstract: The authors derive linear-estimator learnability bounds for cell-type-specific expression and report that deconvolved features can retain prognostic information in a non-small-cell lung cancer survival analysis.
sections.claimed_contribution: For 106 biologically curated cell-type/gene pairs, the authors report that a sparse survival model using deconvolved features predicts overall survival about as well as a model on bulk genes while attributing signals to cell types.
sections.unique_caveat: The 106 targets were found post hoc to have higher learnability; the survival result is an analysis of an existing cohort, not prospective clinical validation or proof of causal cell-type mechanisms.

sections.title: Bayesian Learning of Spatially Heterogeneous Causal Structure in Spatial Transcriptomics
sections.comment: 37 pages, 7 figures. Supplementary Material (56 pages) and Supplementary Atlas (12 pages) are provided as ancillary files. Code: https://github.com/KyungWookBack/SpaDAG
sections.abstract: SpaDAG estimates spatially varying causal DAGs on tissue triangulations, allowing edge direction to reverse across regions; the paper reports simulations and an application to a renal-cell-carcinoma/kidney section.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report improved recovery in simulations, including direction reversals, and identify tumor-region associations in one tissue section as hypotheses for region-specific gene coupling.
sections.unique_caveat: Spatial causal directions in the tumor example are inferred from one section and are not experimentally established mechanisms or validated therapeutic targets.

sections.title: Stochastic Failure Dynamics in a Model Peptidoglycan Mesh under Hydrolysis and Mechanical Loading
sections.abstract: A stochastic-mechanical model of Gram-negative peptidoglycan under hydrolysis predicts weakest-link failure and localized rupture, with mechanical load accelerating collapse in simulations.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors derive limiting failure-time behavior and use stochastic simulations to show that hydrolysis can trigger localized wall collapse even when overall cross-linking remains high.
sections.unique_caveat: The work is a minimal mathematical model, not an experimental demonstration of bacterial lysis under an antibiotic; cellular growth and wall-repair processes are simplified or blocked.

sections.title: Impact of Topology and Sequence Length on the Pressure-Dependent Collapsibility of Proteins
sections.abstract: A theoretical framework with pressure-dependent desolvation predicts that protein topology and sequence length shape pressure-induced collapse into compact, water-mediated conformations.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that increasing pressure destabilizes the fully folded native state while favoring some compact, water-mediated conformations, with effects depending on native topology.
sections.unique_caveat: These are theoretical predictions about collapsibility, distinct from demonstrated folding, function, or experimentally measured pressure response.

sections.title: Trending Research Themes
sections.summary: Selected papers group into biomolecular-interaction modeling, biological prediction and inference across contexts, and genome-analysis infrastructure. These are patterns in this selected corpus, not evidence of field-wide change.

sections.title: Open Problems and Research Directions
sections.summary: Test fast-diffusion and receptor-state model assumptions with direct measurements; experimentally evaluate RNA designs; and stress-test perturbation, deconvolution, and spatial inference across independent donors, datasets, and tissue sections. These are proposed research directions, not clinical advice.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.summary: The clearest shared pattern is methodological: new models address context-dependent molecular interactions and expression. Scores mostly reflect cross-list breadth, not measured popularity; computational predictions still need independent validation.
